chapter: Joe Liggins and back to Kid Ory
title: George Foster versus Tudie Garland; New Orleans bass players
summary: Joe preferred Pops Foster to Tudie for ear and technique, and they discuss great New Orleans bassists and bowing.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: George Foster and Tudie Garland, what was the difference with them? Who did you like to work with?
Oh, I liked George -- by far.
I think George had a better ear and had much more technique than Tudie. That's an easy one for me.

In the bass playing department, there seems to have been a whole bunch of bass players that were a cut above the average, the ones that stayed in New Orleans. People talk about the trumpet players that left New Orleans, and the clarinet players were so much better. But the bass players... Like, you've got Wellman Braud, George Foster, Tudie Garland and Bill Johnson. All of them seem to have been so far in advance... However good they were technically, they seem to be so far in advance of people like Slow Drag and those kind of people, you know.

Oh, well, Slow Drag wasn't in the class of Braud or Pops Foster. Both of these guys got such huge... I listened to the tone, is what I used to like about Pops Foster, and his bowing and things like that.
Nowadays very seldom do you hear any young musicians with a bow. Why has that dropped out, do you think?
Well, it did for a while. But now, Barry, it's kind of coming back. In fact, that bass player that left the band with you, he used a bow all the time.
Yeah. And Red Callender uses his bow a lot.
